root_idea.summary: The root denotes extending, drawing, or pulling something along.
root_idea.development: From the basic action of dragging or drawing, the lexical field develops to tracks and traces, ropes and reins, continued or prolonged actions, things led or pulled, and various specialized and figurative usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized from the imperfect Quranic form to the perfect dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To drag, draw, or pull along.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive action of drawing a person or thing along; the Quranic occurrence has a pronominal object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive camels, sheep, or goats gently while allowing them to graze as they move.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional pastoral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue without interruption, up to the present.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression meaning that something has continued from an earlier time until now.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a continuous track or furrow by movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a numerous army leaving an unbroken track and of horses furrowing the ground with their hoofs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit a crime, offence, or injurious act against someone or oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is understood as bringing the offence upon its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the usual period of pregnancy before giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a female animal or a woman whose pregnancy continues beyond its expected term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become long, said of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of prolonged duration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause lasting rain in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a celestial occurrence said to bring enduring rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To delay or defer someone by repeatedly promising payment later.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may also involve putting off delivery of what is due and drawing the claimant from one place or arrangement to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit an offence or inflict an injury against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical application distinct from the postponement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce someone with a spear and leave it lodged so that it is dragged along.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object left in the victim is the thing being dragged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a rope or halter around someone’s neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The rope is placed upon the neck as an act of leading or restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone or an animal free to pasture or act as they please.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension of making someone drag a rope or halter behind them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To defer payment of a debt, leaving it outstanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of prolonging or drawing something out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sing songs consecutively or without interruption.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singer follows one song with another in succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit a young camel’s tongue and attach a piece of wood so that it cannot suckle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A husbandry operation intended to prevent the weaned animal from nursing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prevent someone from speaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of restraining or drawing back the tongue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a deep, rope-drawn well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use applied to a well whose water is drawn from its depth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be dragged, drawn, pulled, or stretched; to trail along.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or passive-resultative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ruminate or chew the cud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels and other cloven-hoofed animals that bring cud back from the stomach and chew it again.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone authority or power over oneself and submit to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use portraying oneself as subject to being dragged along.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refrain from suckling because of a purulent pustule, ulcer, or similar ailment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a young camel unable or unwilling to nurse because of an ailment in the mouth or elsewhere.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reiterate a cry or bray in the windpipe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of the repeated voice of a stallion-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a repeated noise, cry, or clamour; to produce a sound in the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Extended to beverages or fire that make a sound; the repeated or resonant character is central.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour liquid down the throat or swallow it in successive gulps so that it makes a sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action may be described as making the liquid gurgle in the throat or belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foot, base, or lowest part of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name-like extension of the idea of a lower tract or drawn-out base.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An earthen jar or vessel made of potter’s clay.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also denote an object made generally of clay; its plural includes جِرَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden snare or trapping device for gazelles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The device is a stick with a snare and cord, hidden or set so that the animal becomes entangled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner or mode of dragging, pulling, or stretching.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun sense describing the manner of the action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stomach of a camel or other cloven-hoofed animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the primary anatomical sense recorded for the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cud brought up from an animal’s stomach for chewing or rumination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the cud itself and, by extension, the act of chewing or ruminating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idiomatic expressions, the grievance or matter held in one’s breast and brought into speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Expressions with عَلَى جِرَّتِهِ have variant explanations, including not harboring rancour and not concealing what one has within.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mouthful retained by a camel while it waits for its fodder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal uses the mouthful to occupy itself until feed is brought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female that carries her pregnancy beyond the usual term.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially applied to a she-camel, with detailed terminology for the length of the delay.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel made to incline toward and suckle a young one that is not her own.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A husbandry practice involving the scent of the camel’s milk and the substitution of the young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Refractory and unwilling to be led; or slow-moving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse or camel; the slowness may result from fatigue or shortness of step.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman crippled or unable to walk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by her being dragged along the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep well from which water is drawn by rope, pulley, or draft animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bucket is drawn along the edge of the well’s mouth because of its depth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope, especially a leather nose-rein or neck-cord for a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote a camel’s rope corresponding to a horse’s headstall or rein.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The craft of making jars or earthen vessels; pottery-making.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical occupational or craft noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crime, sin, or punishable offence; an injurious act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the offence a person incurs or brings upon himself or another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Because of someone, on someone’s account, or for someone’s sake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic causal expression originally associated with an offence and extended to general causation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The eel, or a scaleless fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be applied more generally to a fish without scales.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stomach, crop, or craw of a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun synonymous with حَوْصَلَةٌ; it also occurs in an idiom meaning to eat something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who leads a thousand men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional designation based on leading a large body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large, numerous, or heavily marching army or troop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may emphasize the mass of the army or the equipment it drags along.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A potter or maker of jars and earthen vessels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small, yellow female scorpion that drags its tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A highly venomous scorpion, named for its tail-dragging movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron implement or machine used for threshing reaped grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical agricultural term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bean or beans.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal usage reported for the speech of Iraq.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The repeated or gurgling sound made by a camel or by water entering the throat or belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound noun covering the camel’s reiterated cry and the sound of liquid swallowed in successive gulps.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that repeatedly makes loud sounds or brays.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun for a noisy camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of thunder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound-based extension of the repeated roaring or rumbling sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet-smelling plant or herb with a yellow flower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name with no further restriction supplied by the evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large or bulky camel; also a large herd or a complete hundred camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe size, a collected group, or a full counted hundred.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rocket or eruca, including wild and garden varieties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A well-known leguminous plant; the garden variety is distinguished from the wild variety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mill or millstone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the sound made during grinding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that drinks much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually used in the plural expression for camels of this kind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water that makes a noise as it flows or descends.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound-based descriptive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dragging, drawing, or pulling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle of جَرَّ, used adjectivally or substantivally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Violent rain or a torrent that draws along the ground and everything in its path.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression literally evokes a torrent strong enough to draw a hyena from its hole.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Working or burden-carrying camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The camels carry loads or are led by their nose-reins; this is distinct from camels kept for pasturing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: There is nothing in it to attract or profit me.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression in which جَارٌّ denotes an inducement or advantage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain that draws everything along or causes vegetation to grow tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or rare rain-related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large, heavy bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun applied to a bulky bucket of the type called غَرْبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bulky camel or, with feminine marking, a bulky ewe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-descriptive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or route to water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized feminine form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river or rivulet whose bed is formed by a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A watercourse noun derived from the idea of something being drawn or cut along.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The jinn and humankind together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed dual expression for the two classes of beings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or track along which something has been dragged or drawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote the visible trace left by a dragged object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized substantival extension of the place or tract sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beam supporting the ends of rafters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical architectural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Milky Way or a bright tract across the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be conceived as the path of the stars or as a gate or tract in the heavens, named for its resemblance to a dragged track.

cautions: The Quranic form is normalized to the perfect citation form جَرَّ from the supplied imperfect QAC lemma يَجُرُّ.
No Mufradat evidence was supplied for this root; the Quranic sense is consequently limited to the drag, draw, or pull meaning directly supported by the lexical evidence.

The unit discussing rumination is located under Lane entry 46353, whose displayed entry heading is احترّ, while the unit itself explicitly gives the form اجترّ; the rumination meaning is retained under the explicitly stated form اجترّ.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The lexical headword discrepancy between lane:entry:46353 and its g2 unit prevents complete certainty about Lane’s displayed subentry label, although the unit’s explicit form and meaning are clear enough to represent as اِجْتَرَّ.
